subsystems.name: Market data ingestion
subsystems.role: collects real-time prices, order-book depth, news and economic indicators.

subsystems.name: Predictive models
subsystems.role: forecast short-term price moves or market regimes.

subsystems.name: Decision engine
subsystems.role: chooses buy, sell or hold actions to meet an objective.

subsystems.name: Execution system
subsystems.role: places orders in the market with minimal delay.

subsystems.name: Risk management
subsystems.role: caps losses and enforces position and exposure limits.

subsystems.name: Adaptation loop
subsystems.role: updates models as markets change and outcomes are observed.

buildSteps.title: Define the objective and constraints
buildSteps.detail: state what the agent should maximise (e.g. risk-adjusted return), the assets it may trade, and hard limits on leverage and loss.

buildSteps.title: Build the data pipeline
buildSteps.detail: connect to exchange feeds and news sources, clean and align the data into a single real-time stream.

buildSteps.title: Create a simulation environment
buildSteps.detail: model order execution, transaction costs and market impact so the agent can be trained without risking real money.

buildSteps.title: Train the models
buildSteps.detail: use historical data to fit predictive models, then train a reinforcement learning agent inside the simulator to map market states to actions.

buildSteps.title: Backtest rigorously
buildSteps.detail: replay years of market data, including crashes, to check the strategy is not overfitted to past conditions.

buildSteps.title: Paper trade
buildSteps.detail: run the agent on live data without real orders, comparing its decisions against the market and a human baseline.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with guardrails
buildSteps.detail: start with small capital, human oversight and automatic kill switches that halt trading if losses exceed limits.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and retrain
buildSteps.detail: watch for performance drift, data leaks and unexpected behaviour, then retrain on fresh data.

prerequisites.why: agents that react to short-term signals need orders to reach the exchange in milliseconds.
training and backtesting require years of clean price, volume and news data.
works well in games and simulations, but financial markets are noisy, non-stationary and adversarial.
autonomous trading must obey position limits, market rules and audit requirements automatically.
regulators and firms need to understand why an agent took a risky decision, which current deep models rarely provide.

pathway.milestone: algorithmic and high-frequency trading plus robo-advisors automate specific, narrow tasks
pathway.unlocks: faster execution and lower-cost portfolio management under human-designed rules.

pathway.milestone: AI agents that handle multi-step workflows such as rebalancing, tax optimisation and reporting with human sign-off
pathway.unlocks: less manual work for portfolio managers.

pathway.milestone: multi-agent simulations where competing AI traders model market impact and liquidity
pathway.unlocks: better stress-testing of strategies before real capital is risked.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous agents in sandboxed or decentralised markets
pathway.unlocks: continuous, adaptive trading — but only with strong circuit-breakers, because correlated AI behaviour can amplify crashes.
